title: How to Be Better at Lowlight Photography

cards.prompt: Which aperture setting is recommended for lowlight photography?
What does a wide aperture create in the background?
cards.answer: Bokeh, while focusing on a single point.

cards.prompt: You want more background detail. What should you use?
cards.answer: A narrower aperture gives more detail in the background.

cards.prompt: Increasing ISO makes the image cleaner.
cards.answer: Higher ISO brings more light but makes grainier images.

cards.prompt: To reduce grain when using high ISO, use a ____ shutter speed.
Explain like I'm 10: why does a slow shutter speed make photos blurry sometimes?
cards.answer: The camera stays open longer, so if your hands shake or something moves, it gets recorded as blur. A tripod keeps the camera still.

cards.prompt: When using flash, how should you set the exposure?
cards.answer: Under-expose for the preview, because the flash adds light.

cards.prompt: You want to shoot a moving person at night. Slow shutter speed would blur them. What is the trade-off?
cards.answer: Slow shutter speed allows low ISO but blurs movement; fast shutter freezes motion but requires higher ISO (grain) or wider aperture. It is all trade-offs.

cards.prompt: Which is NOT a listed consequence of slow shutter speed?
cards.answer: Bokeh depends on aperture, not shutter speed.
